abstract: The dielectric response of poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) and of PVDF- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> nanocomposites was analyzed in this work. The influence of nano’ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> concentration, between 5 and 30 wt%, on enhancing the dielectric performances of PVDF is discussed in the paper regarding the potential applications of the studied nanocomposites as dielectrics for high energy density polymer capacitors and their use in advanced power systems and electronic devices. The experimental results show that the dielectric spectra emphasize higher real permittivity values for nanocomposites, while the dielectric losses decrease as compared with neat PVDF, especially between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{4}$</tex> Hz. The morphology of the nanocomposites seems to play a significant role in their dielectric behavior.

articleTitle: Study of the Partial Discharge Inception Voltage Variation Over Time on Enameled Wires Subjected to Thermal-Electrical Stress
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The electrical insulation is a crucial element in electrical machines. The performance of the insulation system can be affected by the operating conditions that cause ageing of the insulation. The evaluation of the effects of the environment stresses is a key in the prediction of the electrical insulation breakdown. Being capable of forecasting the maintenance avoiding the out of service due to insulation breakdown is certainly an objective. It is proven that partial discharges (PD) are one of the causes of electrical insulation breakdown. The evolution of PD is an indication of the condition of the electrical insulating system. The severe lowering of the Partial Discharge Inception Voltage (PDIV) value can be a signal of the approaching to the insulation total breakdown. The continuous lowering of the PDIV is due to the degradation of the insulation properties caused by the stresses applied during the operation time. The aim of this study is to evidence and compare the effects of thermal stress on different kind of enamelled wires analysing the PDIV because is one of the accelerating factors together with relative humidity and frequency of the applied voltage [1]–[7]. In this study, twisted pairs made with copper wires covered with different enamels and having thermal class 200°C were assessed. The samples were subjected to thermo-electrical aging tests at the same voltage amplitude and frequency while different temperatures have been applied. The PDIV relevant to the samples was measured regularly to monitor its evolution over time.

articleTitle: Humidity and Temperature Dependences of Resistivities of Various Formulations of Silicone Rubber For HVDC Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Silicone rubber (SiR) is extensively used as housing material for outdoor HV insulators thanks to its excellent long-term stability combined with high hydrophobicity. For HVDC applications, the resistivity of SiR is a key design parameter and knowledge about its changes under various conditions is crucial. In the present work, the influences of relative humidity in air and temperature on the resistivities of five different HTV SiR formulations are studied. The resistivity is calculated from the results of the leakage current measurements conducted on 1.3 mm thick SiR samples under DC voltage. It is found that both the relative humidity and temperature have a significant impact on the resistivity of the studied materials the magnitudes of which varied over several orders. Furthermore, it is observed that SiR formulations with similar composition may have significantly different resistivities under the same temperature and humidity. Accordingly, it is concluded that the resistive properties of each SiR formulation used for HVDC applications need to be carefully evaluated to secure a reliable design and operation.

articleTitle: Wettability, Water Repellent and Anti-Icing Properties of Superhydrophobic and Liquid-Infused Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The icing disaster of transmission lines threatens the safety of power system. Superhydrophobic (SHP) and liquid-infused surfaces (LIS) are two typical new anti-icing surfaces. Herein, the properties of SHP and LIS were compared including wettability, water repellent and anti-icing properties. SHP was prepared by hydrochloric acid (HCI) solution etching and silane modification. LIS was prepared by injecting lubricant into the SHP, and silicone oil was used as lubricant. The aluminum material selected for the aluminum conductor was used as the substrate. Both SHP and LIS exhibit excellent anti-wetting properties and water droplet mobility (SA was about 2°). Notably, LIS has a large adsorption force on water droplets in the direction perpendicular to the surface. The droplet can bounce on SHP, while it can only leave the inclined LIS by slow sliding. Contrarily, LIS exhibits an extremely low ice-adhesion strength, about 1.4 % of SHP, and the ice-adhesion strength increases slowly during the icing/deicing cycles. Therefore, although the SHP exhibits better hydrophobicity and dynamic water repellency than the LIS, the LIS shows better anti-icing performance at low temperatures. This work provides useful information for choosing anti-icing surfaces based on practical applications.

articleTitle: Effect of Residual Traces on Electrical Tree Progress in Silicone Gel
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Our study evaluated the impact of electrical tree traces on the progression of electrical trees within silicone gel. The experimental samples were prepared through pre-voltage application and following subsequent standing periods of either 1 minute or 3 days. The results obtained depicted variations in the electrical trees' advancement depending on the standing duration. Specifically, when the silicone gel was allowed to stand for 3 days, the traces of the electrical trees disappeared, and a wrinkled structure was observed within the sample. Moreover, the initiation voltage for electrical trees increased and the momentary progression was exhibited in the sample.

articleTitle: Effects of Heat and Radiation on the Leakage Current in Silicone-Rubber-Insulated Cables
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Silicone rubber is a keen electrical insulating material for cables used in a nuclear power plant. To evaluate the effects of heat and radiation on the electrical resistivity of the insulation of silicone rubber cables, the leakage current was measured by the current integration method. As a result, it has become clear that the electrical resistivity of the insulation of silicone rubber cables becomes higher when the cables are ex-posed to thermal stresses and gamma-ray irradiation. The rea-son for this seems to be that the transport of ionic carriers becomes difficult as the silicone rubber becomes hardened.

articleTitle: Effect of Lubricant Viscosity on Dynamic Water Repellency and Durability of Lubricated Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Transmission lines icing has seriously threatened the safe operation of power grid. Slippery lubricant-infused porous surface (SLIPS) exhibits excellent antiicing performance, which is a potential candidate in anti-icing field for power transmission lines. However, different lubricant viscosities make the SLIPS exhibit different properties. Herein, the SLIPSs with different silicone oil viscosities were prepared to study the effect of viscosity on the dynamic water repellency and durability of the SLIPSs. The low-viscosity lubricant facilitates the droplet to bounce on the surface, and the droplet slides fast on the inclined surface. Especially, when the viscosity was 20 cSt, the droplet presented superhydrophobic-like bounce on the surface. Additionally, the increase of lubricant viscosity reduces the evaporation loss of SLIPS and improve the lubricant retention rate. When the viscosity was 1000 cSt, most of the lubricant film on the surface still existed after 35 days, and the lubricant retention rate was as high as 69%. Therefore, the low lubricant viscosity enhances the dynamic water repellency of the SLIPS, and high lubricant viscosity is beneficial to the durability of the SLIPS. In practical anti-icing application of lubricated surfaces, the dynamic water repellency and durability of SLIPS should be considered when selecting the lubricant viscosity.

articleTitle: Pre-Breakdown Streamer Phenomena in CO2, Air, and Their Mixtures, and Transition to Leader
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In this study, pre-breakdown phenomena in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, air, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{air}/\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> mixtures are characterized under positive voltage impulses. A point-plane geometry (tip radius of curvature: 0.2mm, inter-electrode distance: 50mm) is used to generate a divergent electric field and facilitate discharge inception. Breakdown voltage measurements and time-resolved discharge characterization are performed for pressure between 0.1 MPa and 0.5 MPa. In air, breakdown results from streamer propagation up to 0.4 MPa, followed by a transition to the leader mode for higher pressures. CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> shows a similar transition above 0.2 MPa, and the mixtures have and intermediate behavior.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Inter-Turn Stresses in Electrical Machines Considering Common Mode Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In the context of the more electric aircraft (MEA), and with the development of hybrid or all electric propulsion systems, future aircrafts will require electrical machines with voltage levels and switching frequencies higher than the reference values of 540 V and 10 kHz, respectively. During voltage transients, windings of electrical machines undergo overvoltages due to waveform reflection phenomena and non-uniform voltage distribution. These phenomena are amplified using modern PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) inverters built with SiC (Silicon Carbine) and GaN (Gallium Nitride) transistors. As a consequence, there is a risk that the inter-turn voltage may be higher than the PDIV (Partial Discharge Inception Voltage). In this context, it becomes crucial to precisely determine these inter-turn voltages. This paper focuses on a High Frequency (HF) model, which aims to predict the inter-turn and turn-to-ground voltages in electrical machines.

articleTitle: Superhydrophobic Coating Prepared by Spraying for Anti-Icing of Glass Insulators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The icing of glass insulators easily triggers flashover, which seriously threatens the safety of power systems. Traditional coatings have poor anti-icing properties and are difficult to be applied in practice. We successfully prepared a superhydrophobic coating on glass slides by one-step spraying. The relationship between spraying pressure, microstructure, wettability and anti-icing performance was investigated. The results indicated that as the spraying pressure increased, the freezing time of the coating first increased and then decreased, while the ice adhesion strength showed a trend of first decreasing and then increasing. This was due to the different rough structures constructed by different spraying pressures. It was found that the coatings prepared at 0.3 MPa had good wettability and anti-icing properties. The contact angle and sliding angle were <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$168.3^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.0^{\circ}$</tex>, respectively. Furthermore, the freezing time and ice adhesion strength were as high as 46.5 min and as low as 55.9 kPa, respectively. This suggests that the prepared superhydrophobic coatings not only retarded icing but also facilitated deicing. It is believed that the present work can provide a reference for the preparation of anti-icing coatings on insulators.

articleTitle: Nanocoating for Variable Frequency Drives Under Square Waveform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: High-voltage transients from inverters have been a significant factor in the early breakdown of insulation in motors powered by inverters, compromising the safety and reliability of variable frequency drivetrains (VFD). Polyimide (PI) films are widely used in enamel wire insulation. Despite the PI films' characteristics of high heat resistance, corona resistance, and other excellent performance, the growing need for higher voltage on electrified transportation demands new and optimized approaches to tackle the concern of premature insulation failure in inverter-fed motors under square waveform. Here, we provide a systematic study of different types of PI films, enhanced with a surface engineering method of 2D nanocoating on the polymer films for improved endurance life under bipolar repetitive square waveform. With the application of 2D inorganic coating by using a readily scalable spray coating method, the time to breakdown of polymer films under repetitive pulse aging is significantly improved. This study contributes to a better understanding of the frequency component under pulse width modulation (PWM) accelerated aging tests and demonstrates the importance of insulating surface engineering, which will contribute to the development of new insulation for the safe operation of variable speed drive (VSD) electric motors with high payload efficiency.

articleTitle: Turn-to-Turn Converter Stress Impact on the Lifetime of Rotating Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The effects of turn-to-turn converter stresses on the lifetime of Litz wires samples have been investigated. Three-level low duty waveshapes have been used to produce a voltage simulating the one appearing during operation. Under such waveform a higher partial discharge inception voltage was recorded. However, no significant improvement in endurance times under discharge was observed, likely due to PD events occurring predominantly at the waveform flanks in converter operation. Corona resistant materials can only partially alleviate the issue, hence PD-free design approaches may be required in many circumstances.

articleTitle: Thermal Equilibrium Composition of C4F7N/CO2 Gas Mixtures During Arc-Interruption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>N/CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas mixtures have been proposed as an eco-friendly insulator with a low global warming potential to replace SF6 in the power grid. However, recent studies revealed that these gas mixtures may decompose in complicated pathways, raising concerns about their scaling-up adoption. In this work, we performed computations aimed at probing the thermal equilibrium composition of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>N/CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas mixtures during arc-interruption based on density functional theory (DFT) and Gibbs free energy minimization. The computations demonstrated that C4F7N stays stable until 1000 K. Above 1000 K, C4F7N rapidly decomposes into CF3, CN, and F free radicals, and the C free radicals released from C4F7N recombine with the O free radicals released from CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to generate CO. Above 10000 K, CO starts to decompose into C free radicals and O free radicals. Above 20000 K, all molecules and free radicals fully decompose into monatomic free radicals, including C, F, N, and O. The computations aid the future mitigation of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>N/CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> decomposition products and promote the adoption of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>N/CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas mixtures in an SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>-free green power network.

articleTitle: Dielectric Performance of Oxidation Ceramic Coating for High Temperature Insulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Advanced surface coating with a high insulation property and good chemical stability is crucial for many electronic and electric systems. However, the insulation property usually sharply decrease under high temperature condition. This undesired phenomenon is a particularly inherent puzzle in well-known used surface coating organic materials. Recently, inorganic surface coating which exhibits excellent dielectric performance and relatively high thermal stability attracts attention for insulation application but the unavoidable porous structure hinders the advanced application. Here, we report a discovery that by forming a hard anodic aluminum oxidation(HAAO) under aluminum and show that it can lead to a high breakdown voltage(3100V) and stable performance up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$200^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, which successfully overcome the long-standing breakdown-stability puzzle in surface coating insulation. Moreover, resistivity dependence of temperature reveals the carrier transportation processing, which is responsible for this combination of high breakdown voltage and good temperature stability. This finding provides an effective approach in surface coating insulation materials with high breakdown voltage and thermal stability.

articleTitle: Research on the Influence of Auto-Reclosing for Grounding Arc Fault in Cable Tunnel Fire Development
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Arc grounding faults of high voltage cables are a strong fire hazard and this is significantly reinforced by auto-reclosing. The simulation of a cable tunnel fire caused by arc fault could help improve the relay protection strategy and fire prevention. The energy release characteristics of the arc were obtained through single-phase arc grounding fault experiment of 110 kV cable. Considering the reclosing process, the average powers of the two arcs are respectively <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.84 \times 10^{4}\text{kW}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.0 \times 10^{4}\text{kW}$</tex>. The large eddy simulation method was used to calculate the smoke flow in fire. The development trend of the fire was analyzed through the temperature distribution. The results show that cables above the fault position heat up rapidly, whereas those below heat up gradually. They both finally reach the ignition point of XLPE and PVC, which are main combustible materials of cable. The highest temperature can reach up to nearly <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$130 0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. Owing to the re-ignition of the arc during auto-reclosing, two peaks were observed in the temperature curves. However, in the longitudinal section of the cable tunnel, a negligible difference was observed in the fire-spreading speed with or without auto-reclosing.

articleTitle: In-Situ Measurement of Surface Charge of a Positive Pulse Surface Discharge in SF6
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Surface discharges in Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_{6}/\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex> mixture threaten the safety of the power system. In the process of a surface discharge, the dynamic surface charge distribution plays an important role to affect and characterize the surface discharge behavior. In this report, the surface charge distribution of a positive pulse surface discharge was measured by the Pockels effect. The measurement was conducted in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_{6}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_{6}/\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex> mixture. The results show that the surface charge gathers around the anode and suppresses the further development of discharge.

articleTitle: A Statistical Approach to Assess the Filler Dispersion of Silicone Rubber Composites for HV Outdoor Insulators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of a statistical analysis for assessing the filler dispersion in silicone rubber composites used for high voltage outdoor insulation applications. The study particularly examines the use of the Median Absolute Deviation as a robust measure to evaluate the variability, and thus repeatability, of thermogravimetric analysis test outcomes for different silicone rubber composites at different temperature rise rates. Different Alumina-trihydrate filled silicone rubber composites are examined in the study. The results suggest a correlation between the Median Absolute Deviation and the degree of filler dispersion observed under Scanning Electron Microscopy. This correlation in outcomes is particularly evident at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25\ ^{0}\displaystyle \mathrm{C}/\min$</tex>. The composites are further tested using the dry-arc resistance test as per ASTM D495. The variability in the erosion resistance outcomes of the dry-arc resistance test correlate with the Median Absolute Deviation outcomes. These outcomes collectively suggest the potential of the proposed statistical approach as a quick assessment tool to supplement microscopic imaging towards understanding the effect of the degree of filler dispersion on the erosion resistance of silicone rubber for use in high voltage outdoor insulation applications.

articleTitle: On-Demand Exfoliation of Boron Nitride Nanosheets for Dielectric Polymer Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Boron nitride nanosheets (BNNSs) have gained extensive attention for nanodielectrics because of their large band gap and ultra-high thermal conductivity. Generally, different electrical applications require different sizes BNNSs. Although sonication-assisted liquid-phase exfoliation (SALPE), the commonly used method, can exfoliate BNNSs from bulk hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) flakes effectively, how to regulate the BNNSs size during SALPE still lack exploration. Herein, based on SALPE, we systematically study the parameters (size of the raw materials, frequency, and power of the ultrasonic source) of BNNSs exfoliation. Then, the exfoliated BNNSs with different sizes were introduced to the polymer matrix. BNNSs with specific sizes among <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.3-5 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> were exfoliated, aiming for different applications. As an example, BNNSs with larger sizes and smaller thicknesses were used to fabricate dielectric nanocomposites with high thermal conductivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(3.9\ \text{Wm}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1})$</tex> and breakdown strength <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(171\ \text{kV mm}^{-1})$</tex> for thermally conductive insulating materials. This work advances our understanding of SALPE and provides an innovative way for exfoliating BNNSs with different sizes for specific applications.

articleTitle: The Impact of Square Wave Ripples Superimposed on HVDC on Electrical Tree Growth in Epoxy Resin
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Power electronic converters are known to introduce harmonics into HVDC transmission systems, so it is critical to understand the effects of these harmonics in polymeric insulation materials. This work considers electrical tree initiation and growth in epoxy resin subjected to +60 kV DC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 10\text{kV}$</tex> square wave and a simple 10 kV bipolar square wave. The average tree initiation time under the bipolar square wave was 40 min, and this was reduced to 12.5 min under +60 kV DC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 10\text{kV}$</tex> square wave. Initial tree channel lengths under bipolar square wave extended typically 60 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, compared to 100 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{x}$</tex> under +60 kV DC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 10\text{kV}$</tex> square wave. For large periods of growth, the HVDC component did not accelerate tree growth, but did lead to more rapid failure. It is argued that the AC component of applied voltage drives tree growth, but ultimately breakdown is controlled by the absolute voltage magnitude.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies of Superhydrophobic Aluminum Conductors by Anodized Etching Method to Improve the Anti-Corrosion Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Atmosphere corrosion inevitably occurs on overhead transmission lines, which causes the hidden dangers of reliability and safety during the service. Coatings technology has not been adopted as the normal countermeasure to protect aluminum conductors. Generally, salt spray for long term often greatly deteriorates the corrosion protection of anti-corrosion coatings. Here, this study proposed superhydrophobic aluminum conductors by anodized etching method to improve the anti-corrosion properties. In addition, anti-corrosion behaviors and mechanisms of prepared aluminum conductors have been studied synthetically.

articleTitle: Aluminum Particles Concentration Effects on Electrical Properties of Metal-Loaded Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The Hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene (HTPB) based composite solid propellants are widely used in rocket and missile propulsion applications. The conductive particles, Aluminum, was dispersed in the composites to improved performance of the solid propellants due to their excellent physicochemical properties. Even though solid propellants are generally considered to be safer than liquid propellants, they are still liable to experience breakdowns under an intense electric field, which may lead to a detrimental loss of properties in their operation. This work is made to understand influence of Aluminum particles concentrations on electrical breakdown, electrical and dielectric properties of HTPB based composites. HTPB based composites with four different concentrations of small size (5 μm) Al particles were prepared. The DC breakdown electric field decreases with increasing the Al particles concentration. Moreover, the presence of these conductive particles induces an increase of permittivity. This fluctuation follows the Maxwell-Garnett approach. However, a decrease of HTPB based composites conductivity was induced by adding metal inclusions, due to the charge trapping effect of Al particles.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Measurement to Predict the Lifetime of High Frequency High Voltage Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: High Frequency/High Voltage Pulsed (HF/HVP) transformers are often used in low power applications. The insulation system is the most critical part of the design because the limited dimensions lead to the presence of high electrical stresses, furthermore the characteristics of the high voltage winding and of the high voltage pulses, result in a not uniform voltage distribution along the winding itself. The high electrical field concentrations require high performance insulating systems including enamels, filled polymers, loaded cast resins. The aim of this work is to implement a tool to be used during the manufacturing process to evaluate the quality of the insulating system as regards the expected lifetime. This tool, based on the partial discharge measurements, should be able to discriminate among HF/HVP transformers having expected lifetimes longer or shorter than a predefined value.

articleTitle: AC Pollution Flashover Characteristics of RTV Coatings with Non-Uniform Aging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: RTV coatings have millimeter-scale non-uniform aging during operation, resulting in non-uniform distribution of hydrophobicity. However, the current research mainly focuses on the centimeter-scale RTV coating damage and does not pay attention to the non-uniform aging phenomenon, and their pollution flashover characteristics are not clear. Therefore, in this paper, a simplified non-uniform aging RTV coating model was designed, hydrophobicity test and artificial pollution flashover test were carried out, and leakage current and flashover process images were recorded. Hydrophobicity tests showed that the dynamic hydrophobicity of non-uniform aging RTV coatings decreased a lot, but still maintained global hydrophobicity. The pollution flashover voltage of the non-uniform aging RTV coating was 8.16 kV, which was 3.8% higher than that of the unaged RTV coating, but the sample variance was large. The leakage current suppression ability of the non-uniform aging RTV coating is reduced, leading to a significant occurrence of spot discharges in the RTV-glass mutation region, which will induce the formation of 4 to 6 dry bands, thereby effectively increasing the pollution flashover voltage. Overall, this study provides insights into the hydrophobicity distribution and pollution flashover characteristics of non-uniform aging RTV coatings.

articleTitle: Surface Engineering Towards Boosted Dielectric Properties for High-Temperature Polymers Under Electrical Extremes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polymer-thin films are critical dielectric materials for capacitive energy storage in power and electronic systems. The rapid development of wide bandgap semiconductors urgently calls for polymers that can attain high energy density and high charge-discharge efficiency at elevated temperatures. However, high-temperature polymers usually suffer from compromised dielectric breakdown strength and soaring conduction loss due to the intrinsic constraint between their bandgaps and thermal stability. In this work, we propose a facile and high throughput interface engineering technique utilizing nanocoatings formed by montmorillonite (MMT) nanoclays, which can serve as an out-of-the-box solution to bypass this constraint. The highly ordered MMT-based nanocoatings with layered structure can significantly block the excessive charge injection at high electric fields and dissipate the charge carriers along the in-plane direction. The MMT-coated PI films exhibit improved breakdown strength, suppressed conduction loss, and boosted charging-discharging efficiency. This work holds the promise of improving the dielectric properties of polymers through surface engineering, enabling their application at concurrent electrical and thermal extremes.

articleTitle: Influence of Irganox 1010 on Space Charge Behavior in Thermal-Oxidatively Aged PP/Elastomer Blends
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polypropylene (PP) has been considered as a promising insulation candidate for high voltage direct current (HVDC) cables for its overall low cost and recyclable. To address its high stiffness limiting application in cable system, a propylene-based elastomer (PBE), DOW VERSIFY™ 2200 was introduced. However, the potential lifetime of blends was confirmed to be reduced dramatically, to only one quarter of that of pure PP. Based on this observation and the fact that antioxidants (AO) can improve the thermal stability, an AO has been introduced to investigate its influence on thermal-oxidative ageing in PP/elastomer blends. According to chemical changes characterized by Fourier-Transform Infrared spectroscopy, the AO reacts with oxygen initially on the sample surface and is assumed to be consumed up within 3 to 4 weeks at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$150 ^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$</tex> in a fan oven. The space charge accumulation behaviour was estimated by the pulsed electro-acoustic method, where a resultant charge peak brought by the AO can be observed resulting in the positive charge movement and negative charge accumulation near the cathode, as a function of the poling time. It has been found that the DC breakdown strength (BDS) shows an increase with ageing times until 4 weeks.

articleTitle: Effect of Fe3O4 and Al2O3 Nanoparticles on AC Breakdown Voltage and Partial Discharge Activity of Synthetic and Natural Esters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper aims to study the impact of conducting (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, 20 nm) and insulating (Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, 20 – 30 nm) nanoparticles (NPs) on the AC dielectric strength and partial discharges activity of synthetic ester MIDEL 7131 (SE) and natural ester FR3 (NE). First, the procedure for preparing nanofluids (NFs), including high-speed agitation and ultrasonication, is presented. Then, the AC breakdown voltage (AC BDV) and partial discharges (PD) activity are measured according to the IEC 60156 and IEC 60270. It is shown that adding Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> NPs improves the AC BDV of SE and NE, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> NPs manifest the best improvement at a concentration (optimal concentration) of 0.4 g/L with SE and NE, while the optimal concentrations for Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> NFs are at 0.3 g/L with SE and 0.2 g/L with NE. In addition, the PD investigation shows that overall, the Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> NPs positively impact the PD performances of SE and NE (except peak charge with NE), while Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> has a positive effect on the PD of SE and NE (except average charge with SE and peak charge with both esters).

articleTitle: Electric Field Measurement in the Process of Partial Discharge Using Electric Field Induced Second Harmonic Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The electric field is critically important in the process of a partial discharge (PD), as it affects many physical parameters such as electron temperature and ion drift velocity. To explore the PD mechanism, the electric field induced second harmonic generation (E-FISH) method, which is an accurate measurement of the transient electric field intensity, is adopted, and one specific electrode configuration is designed to reduce the dispersion of the measurement results. In the sample, an aluminum oxide ceramic sheet is pasted on the metal plane electrode, and a copper foil is pasted on the sheet center, ensuring a uniform electric field distribution between the two copper foils during the PD process no matter where the PD occurs in the channel. The measurement results show that the electric field variation of a PD process among the three measurements is almost the same, with less dispersion in the discharge initiation time, the discharge capacity, and the breakdown electric field.

articleTitle: Influence of Tailored Blend Morphology on Resulting Dielectric Properties in PP-Cast Film
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The investigated approach to increase storage capacity while not compromising dielectric loss or processability is to compliment the properties of a commonly used dielectric polymer, isotactic polypropylene (PP) with a material with higher permittivity, polyvinylidenfluorid (PVDF), in the blend phase. It is known that by a combination of materials with different dielectric constants a common mean value can be achieved. Further, the effect of the shape of inclusions on the resulting permittivity is described in literature. Specifically modified morphologies were processed by shifting the blends into narrow shear rate ranges using skin-layers in multilayer cast film. The complex viscosities were measured to select specific viscosity ratios in the blends and multilayer films. The development of the morphology was examined in extruded cast film via laser scanning microscopy (LSM) and dark field microscopy in respect to filler content, viscosity ratios and layer-structure. The shown rheological influence on the morphology is in good agreement with the theoretical expectations. The elongation of blend particles was suppressed when extruding blends in the core of multilayer cast films with low viscosity skin-layers. The resulting relative permittivity of blends was calculated using the Maxwell-Garnett approximation with form factors that take into account how the structure and internal geometry of the mixture affect permittivity. The measured relative permittivity increased for specimen with a mainly spherical blend phase, which is in good agreement with the mathematical EMA model.

articleTitle: AC Impedance Spectroscopy to Characterize the Dielectric Material Properties in Concrete During Decommissioning of Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is a powerful technique to study material properties, e.g., it is highly sensitive to the moisture content of inhomogeneous cementitious materials. This study contributes to the in-situ measurement of the moisture content (MC) in concrete during the decommissioning of nuclear power plants. Thus, a comprehensive investigation of dielectric material properties of concrete has been performed experimentally and over a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10{{\ Hz}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10\text{MHz}$</tex> range of frequencies through alternating current (AC) impedance spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Evidence of Negative Differential Resistance in Solid Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper investigates the possibility for solid dielectrics used for HVDC applications to exhibit a regime of negative differential resistance (NDR) under electric fields close or within typical operating conditions. Peculiar experimental evidence arises from space charge measurements on nano-filled polypropylene, where charge transport seems to occur in a direction that is opposite to what is normally expected. Extensive experimental investigation on space charge accumulation at different fields allowed for a rough estimation of the electric fields of NDR regime, assessed between 18 and 28 kV/mm, supporting the initial hypothesis, and possibly related to the nature of functionalized nanofillers in the material.

articleTitle: Semi-Interpenetrating Polymer Blend Exhibit Stable Energy Storage Performance at High Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Recently polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) based polymers present attractive energy storage performance, however, the inherent pool temperature stability could lead to deteriorated energy storage performance or even thermal runaway, which should be ascribed to vulnerable amorphous regions under elevated temperature. Here we propose a strategy to enhance the temperature stability of polymer blends by interpenetrating high-polarization PVDF-based polymers and high-glass-transition-temperature polymer matrices PMMA. The dielectric properties of the interpenetrating blends are studied and compared with solution blends. When properly engineered, the interpenetrating polymer blends exhibit an appreciated energy density of about 6. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\sim 7.6\mathrm{J}/\text{cm}^{3}$</tex> over a wide temperature range from room temperature to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$120^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Stress Limitation in the Coil Heads of Electrical Machines Using Optimized Winding Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The supply voltage of electrical machines tends to be increased, both in industrial applications and in electro-mobility uses. As a result, the Electrical Insulation System (EIS) must be adapted accordingly to these constraints. Defining the EIS requires knowing accurately the critical voltage levels that appear in the motor. For a concentrated winding fed by a Variable Speed Drive (VSD), the highest stresses occur in the slots. However, for distributed windings, as in conventional induction or synchronous machines, the most critical stresses appear in the coil heads, whether they are supplied by an inverter or by the grid. The objective of this study is to investigate possible solutions able to limit these constraints.

articleTitle: Flexible Polyolefin with Enhanced Dipolar Polarization for Energy Storage Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polymer dielectrics endowed with high dielectric constant and high breakdown strength are critical for high-power systems and compact electronics to realize ultrahigh energy density. Nevertheless, the constrained energy density attainment of prevalent commercial polymers such as BOPP has been impeded by their inadequately satisfied dielectric constant. A polynorbornenes-BP (PNB-BP) is introduced in this paper, which features a rigid backbone composed of bicyclic aliphatic, while the incorporation of an electron acceptor and aromatic groups facilitates the formation of an enhanced dipole, endowing it with a satisfied dielectric constant of 3.72. Leveraging its high breakdown strength, the PNB-BP polymer achieves a notable energy density of 12.7 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at room temperature. Furthermore, the PNB-BP polymer exhibits commendable thermal properties, including a high glass transition temperature (Tg) of 220°C, and satisfactory thermal stability as evidenced by the observed dielectric constants. The design strategy uncovered in this work unveils the to realize the ultrahigh energy density of the capacitor by introducing the enhanced dipole.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Measurement for Low- Voltage Motor Insulation Systems at Square Wave Voltage with Variable Slew Rate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In this work the dependence of the repetitive partial discharge inception voltage on the slew rate at square wave voltage is investigated. The partial discharge (PD) is measured with high frequency current transformers in combination with high pass filters and a wide band digital oscilloscope. A silicone carbide inverter is presented to generate the test voltage. The developed gate driver makes it possible to vary the slew rate. Twisted pairs are used as test samples, which are a possibility to represent the insulation system of the winding head of an electric motor. The results show that for unimpregnated twisted pairs a self-healing effect occurs, which is most likely due to the formation of space charges in the air winding. In comparison, the influence of the slew rate is rather negligible in the range considered.

articleTitle: The Mutual Influence of Relaxational and Induced Polarization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In dielectrics, relaxational polarization by permanent dipoles and polarization by induced dipoles may exist in parallel. Both polarizations can interact by their dipole fields influencing the total polarization. A computer aided method to calculate this polarization is developed. The method is based on repeated runs atom by atom through the system combining deterministic field calculations and probabilistic Monte Carlo steps. The impact of thermal vibrations is considered.

articleTitle: Influence of Voltage Overshoot in Enamel Wire Winding Insulation Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The voltage level used in electrical vehicles increase continuously which can be used to improve system efficiency. As the rise time decrease, the probability for overshoots in the voltage waveform however increases. The presence of overshoots increases the stress on the insulation system, particularly when partial discharge (PD) activity is introduced in the insulation. This work focus on elaborating the influence of voltage overshoot magnitude on enamel motor wire insulation with different insulation conductivity, utilizing different rise times and DC magnitudes. An approach and evaluation method to explore the performance of the insulation system is presented and demonstrated in this work. The measurement results show that the two specimens differed in the summed magnitude of PDs measured at the different flanks for all voltage levels, which is an indicator that the presence of overshoot can influence the stress level differently. Also, lower voltage levels utilizing shorter rise times can result in higher PD exposure than significantly larger ones with longer. The paper thus recommends that waveshapes which as much as possible resembles the stress in the actual application is used during insulation and product evaluations and consider the possibility for overshoots.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Stress Grading System of Medium Voltage Motors Fed by Adjustable Speed Drives Under Elevated Ambient Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Today's stress grading system (SGS) used in medium voltage and high voltage motors is a combination of SiC based stress grading tape (SGT) and conductive armor tape (CAT). SGS., also identified as the corona protection system., has been developed to have good field grading properties and low temperature rise at operations under normal power frequency voltages. However, a converter voltage containing pulses with short rise time and high repetition frequency will affect the temperature distribution along the SGS. The available length and thickness of CAT and SGT, conductivity of CAT, conductivity/nonlinearity of SGT, are parameters that can be adjusted for effective stress grading systems. This paper presents an optimization strategy for the CAT length to reduce temperature rise along the end winding region for motors operating in elevated ambient temperatures.

articleTitle: Optimization of Corona Triode Polarization by 2D Electrostatic Mapping
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Traditional methods for characterizing piezoelectric materials typically involve analyzing their electromechanical response, focusing on coefficients such as the piezoelectric strain coefficient d33. In this study, an alternative approach is proposed to evaluate the piezoelectric response by examining the surface charge accumulated in the tested sample following a corona polarization process. Through the use of an electrostatic voltmeter, two influential factors affecting the piezoelectric response were investigated: the number of needles employed during the polarization and the presence of a grid interposed between the high-voltage needles and the specimen.

articleTitle: Space charge and polarization in insulators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Space charge and polarization effects have been observed since as early as antiquity. They have been associated during these millennia with the development of physics and particularly electromagnetism. Today they are involved in beneficial applications such as electrets. However, they also have negative consequences such as in high voltage insulation. This latter field is of particular importance since the reduction in the global carbon footprint will lead to a strong development in the use of electricity. Other applications of insulators and their polarization are now under development in novel fields, such as neural networks, biology and microfluidics, for instance using electrophoresis when dealing with charged particles or using dielectrophoresis when dealing with uncharged particles such as cells at microscale. Examples will be given of such new applications.

articleTitle: Parametric Simulation Study of High-Energy Ultrasonic Nondestructive Assessment for Filler Dispersion in Nano-Modified
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The insulation performance of the modified nanomaterials is critical to the safety and stability of the next-generation low-carbon power transmission system, while the dispersion of nanofillers in the dielectrics directly affects the electrical/mechanical/thermal properties. The existing methods for particle dispersion detection in solid polymeric materials are mainly microscopic imaging methods, however, they have a shortage of narrow detection areas and cannot evaluate the material dispersion as a whole. In this paper, we use high-power ultrasonic methods to measure the nonlinearity of different dispersive nanomaterials. To achieve accurate measurement and evaluation, quantitative optimization of excitation signal parameters is the key to high-power ultrasonic detection. Firstly, the nonlinear acoustic fluctuation equations of solid nanocomposite are derived based on the nonlinear acoustic theory. After that, a filler mass fraction of 1% with different agglomeration degrees was modeled and simulated to optimize the excitation ultrasonic parameters. The simulation results show that in the system of epoxy resin-silica particles (mass fraction 1%), the nanomaterial nonlinear coefficient increases by a maximum of 2% with the increase of particle agglomeration, and the dispersion decreases significantly; The optimal frequency range of the excitation signal is 0.1 MHz-5 MHz, and the optimal vibration amplitude is 70 nm. In this paper, the simulation studies accomplish parametric validation of the nonlinear model, preliminarily select the optimal frequency range for signal excitation, determine the optimal amplitude size of the excitation signal, and provide theoretical guidance for the optimal design of the high-energy ultrasonic measurement device.

articleTitle: Pollution Deposition and Pollution Flashover Characteristics of Superhydrophobic Surface in DC Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Superhydrophobic coatings have gained extensive attention for external insulation because of their self-cleaning properties and high electrical insulation properties. Generally, with the hydrophobicity of external insulation equipment surface improving, the surface pollution deposition can be effectively reduced, so as to improve the anti-pollution flashover performance. Herein, based on a natural pollution accumulation system, we systematically study the macroscopic and microscopic characteristics of the pollution deposition for superhydrophobic surface. Then, the effect of different equivalent salt deposit density on pollution flashover voltage for superhydrophobic surface was studied. With the increase of hydrophobicity, the pollution distribution on the different hydrophobicity surface changes from chain to cluster, which can increase the pollution flashover voltage. The pollution flashover on superhydrophobic surface has competition mechanism, which can lead to the failure of anti-pollution flashover performance in severely pollution environment.

articleTitle: Performance of Micro-Varistor Stress Grading in Cable Terminations Subjected to Repetitive Fast Transients
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In this study, a commercial cable termination that employs micro-varistor stress grading is subjected to repetitive impulse voltages, to assess the associated temperature rise. Additionally, a COMSOL® model is developed to further investigate the effectiveness of micro-varistor stress grading on the electric field distribution. The measured and simulated results provide confirmation of the effectiveness of the micro-varistor stress grading cable termination when exposed to repetitive impulse voltages.

articleTitle: Study on Corona Onset Voltage of Parallel Rod Electrodes Under AC-DC Combined Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: To study the influence of climate factors on corona discharge under AC-DC combined voltage, it is required to build an artificial climate chamber. AC and DC voltage will be introduced into the chamber by parallel wall bushings. To prevent corona discharge between the bushings, the variation law of corona onset voltage of parallel rod electrodes under AC-DC combined voltage should be explored. Four-channel acquisition card and low potential measurement method were ultilized, rod radius, distance between two rods and AC/DC ratio were changed to get the corona onset voltage. The corona onset voltage at DC side and AC side both increased with the increase of rod radius and the distance between two rods. Under the same fixed voltage component, the order of the corona onset voltage from the largest to the smallest is: the negative half cycle corona at AC side, the positive half cycle corona at AC side, the negative corona at DC side, and the positive corona at DC side. Therefore, it is particularly important to pay attention to the situation where positive DC-AC voltage is introduced, and the corona discharge is most likely to occur at DC side.

articleTitle: Dielectric, Thermal and Mechanical Properties of a Sequence-Regulated Ethylene/Anisylpropylene Copolymer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The copolymerization of ethylene and anisylpropylenes by a sterically demanding half-sandwich scandium catalyst afforded an entirely new class of copolymers with a wide range of glass-transition temperatures (Tg) and mechanical, self-healing, and shape-memory properties by controlling the comonomer sequence and polymer molecular weight and varying the anisyl substituents. This paper focuses on the dielectric, thermal and mechanical properties of one representative of this class of copolymers to investigate its potential for use in electrical insulation technology. Dielectric, thermal and mechanical properties were comprehensively evaluated for the above copolymer. Besides estimating volume and surface resistivity and dielectric strength, the temperature and frequency dependence of the relative permittivity and loss factor were studied. Tg was also determined by differential scanning calorimetry. Tensile tests assessed mechanical and self-healing properties. The tested copolymer has excellent dielectric parameters that can be compared with commonly used insulating materials. Below the observed T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>, the material also shows satisfactory electrical insulation properties in the frequency domain. The results of tensile tests show that the copolymer's stress-strain curve has a typical trend for thermoplastic polymers. In the range of elastic deformations, the material offers non-autonomous self-healing properties.

articleTitle: Investigation on Compatibility of Insulating Materials in On-Load Tap Changer with Insulating Oil
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The insulation system of On-load tap changer (OLTC) is composed of insulating oil and the solid insulating materials in OLTC. The compatibility of solid insulating materials in OLTC with mineral insulating oil is one of the most important factors to decide the long-term reliable operation of OLTC. However, the compatibility of OLTC insulating components with mineral insulating oil is seldom studied. In this work, the effect of insulating materials, such as Epoxy Phenolic Glass Cloth Laminates (EPGCL3248), Epoxy Glass Fiber (EGF), Reinforced Nylon (PA66), Polyformaldehyde (POM) on the electrical and physicochemical properties of insulating oil were analyzed. The solid insulating materials were immersed in 800 mL insulating oil separately, and aged at 90 ºC, 100 ºC, 110 ºC, and 130 °C. The aging time is 20 h, 41 h, 82 h, and 164 h, respectively. After the thermal aging, the water content, breakdown voltage, dielectric loss and acidity of insulating oil samples were tested, and the compatibility between the insulating oil and the solid insulating materials was analyzed. Among the solid insulating materials used in OLTC, the Nylon PA66 exhibits poor compatibility with mineral oil. The research results provide useful advises for the selection, optimization and replacement of OLTC solid insulating materials.

articleTitle: Electrical Treeing Simulations to Understand the Applicability of Needle-Plane Tests to Cables
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Electrical treeing in lab-based testing currently requires the use of field enhancement points such as needle tips or thin wires. While these techniques produce reliable electrical tree growth, it is important to understand the limitations of such tests in the context of the different geometries found in high voltage assets. Here we apply Finite Element Analysis tools to investigate the consequences of using needle-plane geometries and to develop ideas on how treeing within a more uniform field may relate or differ. This work finds that local geometrical effects present in non-conductive trees in more uniform systems, responsible for variation in field magnitudes are unlikely to be replicated in needle-plane tests.

articleTitle: Correlation of Gas Generation Characteristics with Partial Discharge Energy in an Insulating Liquid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Dissolved gas analysis (DGA) is one of the most important techniques to detect incipient electrical and thermal faults in liquid-filled transformers. It is well known that different gases or gas patterns correspond to specific fault types. For example, hydrogen (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is recognized as the key gas of partial discharges (PD) in insulation liquids. However, few studies have been able to accurately quantify the relationship between gas generation characteristics and PD energy because of possible issues with hydrogen (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) leakage during the test, sampling, and measurement processes. It is therefore not clear how the PD energy and PD magnitude affect the gas generation characteristics. This work aims to investigate the effects of PD magnitude on gas generation rate, the volume of gas generated per unit PD energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mu \mathrm{L}/\mathrm{J})$</tex>, in a mineral oil using a gas tight test system. Gas generation experiments using different PD magnitudes over durations up to 96 hours have been performed. The results show that a higher PD magnitude test results in a higher rate of hydrogen gas generation.

articleTitle: Life Estimation of MIND HVDC Cables Subjected to Qualification Tests Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study aims at estimating for the first time the life in HVDC Mass-Impregnated Non-Draining MIND cables subjected to Prequalification Test (PQT) conditions according to CIGRE Technical Brochure 853:2021. A MATLAB simulation is carried out to calculate temperature and electric field distribution within MIND insulation during PQT Load Cycles, and to estimate cable insulation life under PQT conditions. The results show that estimated life of MIND cables under PQT conditions is far longer than the duration of the PQT (360 days), as well as longer than that previously estimated under the same conditions for extruded cables.

articleTitle: Effect of Measurement Temperature on Electrical Cable Frequency Domain Reflectometry Response
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In nuclear power plants, electrical cables are exposed to stressors, such as elevated temperature and radiation. Evaluation of the effect of stressors on the condition of electrical cables can be conducted using offline electrical reflectometry techniques, such as frequency domain reflectometry (FDR). However, recent work has raised the concern that FDR measurements at temperatures higher than ambient may diminish or reduce the response due to stressors, potentially leading to incorrect assessment of electrical cable damage. In this work, we explore the FDR response of an electrical cable exposed to an oven-based thermal stressor up to 140°C, including both ramping up and ramping down temperature. It was observed that, for both the oven entrance and exit, an increase in the FDR measurement temperature led to a decrease in the FDR reflection coefficient. In particular, it was found that the reflection coefficient at the oven entrance decreased from the ambient measurement by approximately 7%, 22%, and 36% at temperatures of 60°C, 100°C, and 140°C, respectively.

articleTitle: Modeling PEA Measurements of Arbitrary Layered Dielectrics Using the Ray-Trace Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Layered dielectrics have increasingly been investigated as insulators for high voltage power applications. Pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) measurements on layered materials can be difficult to interpret because of the net bound charge at each dielectric interface and acoustic reflections that occur at each interface. The ray-trace model is a useful technique to determine the source of peaks in each waveform because the path of each acoustic wave (ray) is explicitly traced during the modeling process. In this work we implement the ray-trace method to model PEA measurements of arbitrary layered dielectrics. We have developed a “random walk” method to find all unique rays that begin at a charge layer, end at the sensor, and travel an arbitrary path through the layered dielectric material. The quantity of charge at each dielectric interface was determined by first calculating the bound charge for each material based on the electric field present, then calculating the net bound charge at each interface. The arrival time and relative amplitude of peaks in the arriving waveform are then calculated directly from the rays, material properties, and calculated charge. PEA measurements were done on layered dielectric materials. Collected waveforms were compared with those calculated using the ray-trace model. Results showed good agreement in peak amplitude and location between measured and calculated waveforms.

articleTitle: Study on Space Charge Accumulation in Silicone Rubber Encapsulant Under DC Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Silicone rubber is a kind of polymeric insulating material commonly used in power electronic device encapsulation. The insulation performance of encapsulant directly determines the operating reliability of power electronic devices. Under DC voltages, space charge accumulation will directly affect short-time breakdown characteristics and long-term aging properties of the insulation. This paper carried out experimental measurement on space charge based on pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) method for revealing space charge characteristics in silicone rubber encapsulant. The experimental samples were prepared using two curing processes. And further comparative experiments were also conducted to explore the effect of post-curing on space charge characteristics in silicone rubber encapsulant.

articleTitle: Evolution Impact of Electrical Insulation Systems in High Power Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The paper deals with the history and evolution of electrical insulation systems, beginning with the discovery of insulation with the first experiments on electricity. Then, the aim is to analyses the use of insulation in electrical machine windings and the definition of the different parameters for the characterization. Thereafter, this paper compares the thermal performance of the turn-to-turn insulation in several historic periods to demonstrate their improvements and the possible impact on the machine's sizing.

articleTitle: Simulation of PD RF Propagation in MV Bus Bar Chambers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The monitoring of partial discharge (PD) in air-insulated medium voltage (MV) switchgear can reveal potential insulation failure. In particular, the application of non-intrusive methods such as radio frequency (RF) sensors may be employed to establish continuous PD level tracking. However, there is still clarification needed to understand the most effective placement of RF probes, especially along extended MV switchgear compartments. Therefore, the aim of the current work is to investigate PD RF signal propagation and signal energy sensitivity along three aligned arbitrary MV switchgear bus bar compartments. A particular model was created by applying finite element methods (FEM) and a grid of probes is created along the chamber structures. By using calculation methods and creating interpolation maps, the potential higher measurement sensitivity regions can be revealed for different PD source locations.

articleTitle: Electrical and Optical PD Measurements with Si3N4 Power Electronics Substrate Embedded in Silicone Oil
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental study of partial discharges (PD's) carried out with a Silicon Nitride Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> substrate embedded in silicone oil. Optical PD detection is feasible with such non-electroluminescent materials, and can be done whatever the shape of applied voltage (dc, ac, fast impulses), whereas conventional electrical PD measurements can be obtained only with ac or dc. Optical PD recordings show that PD inception is greatly favoured under fast rise impulse compared to ac. The influence of pulse risetime and dc prestress shows that PD inception is strongly influenced by space charge injection, in the case of slow high voltage waves such as ac or dc.

articleTitle: Investigation of $\mathrm{S}{\mathrm{i}}_3\ {\mathrm{N}}_4$ Nanoparticles Effect on the Electrical Properties of Polyimide for Power Electronics Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In this article, the electrical characterization of nanostructured polyimide (PI) films is presented. The addition of silicon nitride <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\mathrm{S}{\mathrm{i}}_3\ {\mathrm{N}}_4})$</tex> as nanoparticles ensures an enhanced thermal conductivity and high temperature endurance of PIs, without worsening their electrical performances. The effect of different concentrations of nanoparticles on the base PI is investigated by means of broadband dielectric spectroscopy and thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC).

articleTitle: A method to detect mechanical cracks creation and/or propagation in insulators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Fracto-emission is the ejlection of electrons and positive ions from mater subjected to a mechanical fracture. The mechanical fracture is accompanied by the creation and/or the propagation of cracks in the mater, leading to a succession of fracto-emissions. First, we have described, through analytical equations, the amount of surface charge produced by a mechanical fracture and how it can be measured with an external measuring circuit. Then, this measuring device is used to detect the appearance of cracks and their propagation under mechanical stress. This method allows to study the electro-mechanical interactions, particularly for insulators for which the electromechanical breakdown model is being considered.

articleTitle: Effect of Surface Treatment of Halloysite Nanotubes on the Properties of LLDPE/HNT Composites for the Cable Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polymer composites based on linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) and halloysite nanotubes (HNTs) are promising for low fire-hazard cables (LFHC) due to their proven fire-retardant properties. This work aims to describe changes in dielectric, thermal and mechanical parameters for LLDPE/HNT composites that differ in the surface treatment of the incorporated HNT particles. Two sets of LLDPE/HNT composites containing 5 wt% of incorporated HNTs with and without surface treatment by stearic acid were prepared by extrusion. The LLDPE without filler was selected as the reference material. Measurement of selected dielectric properties, tensile tests and thermal properties by simultaneous thermal analysis and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) were performed. Adding HNTs or their subsequent modification did not significantly affect the mechanical properties. It is also evident that the addition of unmodified HNTs shifted the main thermo-oxidative peak on the DSC signal to the higher temperatures; thus, HNTs positively reduced the maximum heat flow and enthalpy distribution of the whole system. Unfortunately, the effect of surface treatment of HNTs with stearic acid is the opposite. The dissipation factor increases over the range of measured temperatures and frequencies. However, the surface modification of HNTs slightly reduced the dissipation factor for some frequencies and temperatures. It is clear from the presented results that the chosen type of surface modification of HNTs is not as beneficial as the addition of unmodified HNTs.

articleTitle: Vertically Printed Ferroelectret Microstructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Using fused filament fabrication, ferroelectrets (i.e. polymer films with internal air-filled voids) can be manufactured from a variety of materials and with custom designed structures for optimum mechanical compliance and piezoelectric activity. In this study, we investigated a vertically oriented “double-wave” design, which results in structures with very low mechanical stiffness, and hence high piezoelectric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{33}$</tex> coefficients. The structures were designed in an open-source parametric modeler and 3D-printed from polylactic acid (PLA) and polypropylene (PP). The total thickness is approx. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$300 \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> and channel void heights are around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. When charged in direct contact, the ferroelectret samples exhibited a remanent polarization of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.25 \text{mC}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex> (PP) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.12 \text{mC}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex> (PP), respectively. Piezoelectric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{33}$</tex> coefficients of up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$800 \text{pC}/\mathrm{N}$</tex> were observed, but showed a strong decrease when static bias forces in excess of 1 N were applied to the 16 mm diameter electrodes. This behavior is likely caused by a stiffening of the double-wave structure as more compressive stress is applied. FEM calculations showed a very low effective Young's modulus of 125 kPa.

articleTitle: Effects of Temperature and Pressure on the Dielectric Properties of Plasma Sprayed Alumina Coatings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Dielectric spectroscopy at different pressure and temperature levels can provide crucial quantitative information on the properties of various insulating materials. Thermally sprayed ceramic coatings have the potential to be used in high temperature applications where conventional polymers are not suitable to retain their electrical insulation. In the present study, alumina <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{A}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3})$</tex> coatings have been prepared on copper substrates by atmospheric plasma spraying. Different gas mixtures containing varying levels of hydrogen were utilized to assess the significance of energy input on coatings. The samples were tested by dielectric spectroscopy at temperatures ranging from −50 to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$150^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and different pressure levels in the frequency range of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> Hz to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> Hz.
