It was discovered that temperature increases both the dielectric constant and loss tangent at low frequencies. Moreover, the microstructure of the coatings has been linked to the dielectric behavior. The primary polarization mechanism at low frequencies is determined as space charge polarization, which is highly affected by different temperature and pressure levels. The results of our study offer valuable insights for the design of next-generation electrical insulation systems utilizing ceramic coatings.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Modeling and Calculation of the Electric and Thermal Field Distribution in Composite Insulators with Different Types of Defects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In recent years, several incidents of abnormal heating in composite insulators have been witnessed during operation, which is regarded as the early stage of FRP rod degradation. The abnormal heating behavior generally stems from the increase of leakage current inside the composite insulators, and the increased current density is closely related to the specific defects or failures located in different domains. This paper deals with several types of defects in composite insulators, calculates the current density distribution in each case with a three-dimensional finite element model, and analyzes the concentration areas of local electric field or current density. Potential partial discharge and local heating behaviors are analyzed. It is also concluded that the radial current in the silicone rubber sheath caused by the distorted potential distribution along the degraded rod-sheath interface is one of the possible reasons for the lateral punch holes in the failed silicone rubber sheath. This study provides theoretical support in failure identification of composite insulators based on the IR thermal detection.

articleTitle: Dielectric Permittivity and Breakdown Strength of Thermally Aged Polypropylene/Ultra–High Molecular Weight Polyethylene Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study investigates the effects of thermal aging on PP/UHMWPE blends and PP/UHMWPE/MgO nanocomposites. Thermal degradation of the aged materials is evaluated using thermogravimetric analysis, showing a reduction in the onset degradation temperatures for both systems. PP/UHMWPE/MgO demonstrates better thermal stability than PP/UHMWPE. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy is employed to analyze the surface chemical modifications in the aged samples. The findings indicate the formation of carbonyl groups, with PP/UHMWPE/MgO displaying lower rates of oxidation compared to PP/UHMWPE. Relative permittivity increases with aging time, but the increase is less pronounced in the PP/UHMWPE/MgO. The presence of a dielectric relaxation peak at varying frequencies, with PP/UHMWPE exhibiting higher frequencies, is observed. AC breakdown strength gradually decreases with increasing aging time in both sample types, albeit to a lesser extent in the nanocomposites. Overall, the study demonstrates that the addition of MgO in PP/UHMWPE nanocomposites under thermal aging has a mitigated impact on thermal stability, oxidation reactions, dielectric permittivity, and AC breakdown strength when compared to PP/UHMWPE blends.

articleTitle: Quantification of Electric Field Distortion around an Asymmetric Agglomerate Using 3D Reconstruction of TiO2/Epoxy Nanocomposite
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The breakdown strength of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/epoxy nanocomposites is dependent on the equivalent sphere diameter of the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticle agglomerates. However, the actual agglomerates have asymmetrical shapes. Quantifying the electric field distortion and the induced trap depth around the asymmetric agglomerates is crucial for discussing the breakdown mechanism. This paper describes the method for quantifying the electric field distortion and the induced trap depth around an asymmetrical agglomerate model, which was obtained from a 3D reconstruction of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/epoxy nanocomposite.

articleTitle: Optical Measurement Method of Electromechanical Effect Based on Fabry-Perot Interference Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The detection of electromechanical effect plays a vital role in the accurate calibration of wearable devices, microrobots, and nano-electromechanical systems. A high-precision microstrain detection system based on fiber Fabry-Perot (F-P) interference for obtaining precise electromechanical coupling coefficient was established in this article. In light of the structural characteristics of the F-P interferometer, piezoelectric (PZT) was selected as core material embedded in the sensor for forming an optical fiber F-P cavity. The deformation of the sample was detected from the wave shift in the interference spectrum by the system under step voltages. As demonstrated by the results, the fitting degree is obtained between the deformation of the sample and electric field strengths as high as that the coefficient of determination (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is 99.97%. The measured resolution could reach to the level of 10 pm in the meantime.

articleTitle: An Elastomeric Coating for Large-Scale Deicing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Icing on the surfaces such as overhead conductors, insulators, aircraft and wind turbine blades interferes with social stability and people's tranquility. Superhydrophobic and super-lubricated coatings, which are considered as potential anti-icing technologies, face the limitation that ice adhesion force increases with icing area. In this work, polyurethane elastomer coatings with different PTFE mass fractions were successfully prepared on aluminum plates. The microscopic morphology, wettability and large-scale deicing performance of the coatings were studied. The results indicated that the coating surface gradually became rougher due to the increase of PTFE addition. As the PTFE mass fraction increased, the deicing force of the coatings showed a trend of first decreasing and then increasing. Compared with the coating without PTFE (114.1 N/cm), the coating with 10% PTFE mass fraction measured a constant deicing force as low as 96.1 N/cm. Moreover, it was found that the critical length of the coating was reduced by the addition of PTFE, which was beneficial to the realization of large-scale deicing. The coatings based on polyurethane elastomers with the addition of PTFE show good potential for large-scale deicing of power transmission lines.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of the Electric Field in HVDC GIL Considering Defects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: HVDC GIL is a suitable transmission technology in power systems, due to its advantages in power capacity, compact structure and reliability. However, inappropriate manufacturing and incorrect installation may cause defects within the GIL, e.g. metallic particles in the insulating gas or pits or protrusions at the spacer. The defects may lead to enhanced electric field stress, which may result in partial discharge or system failure. Thus, the effect of the defects need to be determined and therefore the electric field distortion by various defects within the GIL is examined by application of different numerical simulation models to obtain exact simulation results.

articleTitle: Electrical Treeing Morphologies and Behaviors Discovered in Aerospace-Grade Fluorinated Ethylene Propylene
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Electrification is on the forefront of research among many industries to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions. To electrify an aircraft, insulation materials are required to handle high operational voltages as well as extreme conditions for the entirety of the aircraft life. Unfortunately, polymer dielectrics are prone to an aging phenomenon called electrical treeing. Electrical treeing can cause electrical breakdown in insulation systems because it propagates through-thickness. This phenomenon has never been studied in aerospace grade dielectric materials before. Not only is it crucial to understand this aging mechanism in aerospace grade materials before service introduction, but it is also imperative to understand how aircraft operating conditions, like temperature and pressure, affect it. This study reveals that commercially available, aerospace-grade, fluorinated insulation material (Fluorinated Ethylene Propylene) is prone to a type of treeing not yet discovered. Additionally, it is shown in this work that the directionality of this dielectric could be leveraged to mitigate electrical tree growth, which would be an elegant, cost-effective solution for preventing electrical treeing in aircraft systems.

articleTitle: Influence of Multi-ageing on Electrical Properties of Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Dry-type film capacitors are the core equipment for smart grids and new energy power generation, and their performance greatly depends on the insulation properties of the internal biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films. In this paper, multi-physics field aging equipment is applied to conduct electrical-thermal-mechanical aging of BOPP films, and the crystallization characteristics, dielectric properties and trap characteristics of aged BOPP films are studied. The results show that the crystalline form of BOPP film will not change during aging, but shallow traps will be introduced inside, which will promote the decay of surface potential and increase space charge injection. Meanwhile, properly increasing the tensile force (30 N to 40 N) of the BOPP film during electro-thermal aging will increase the dielectric constant and reduce the dielectric loss tangent of the BOPP film, hence restoring the dielectric properties of the BOPP film.

articleTitle: Anti-Icing Performance of Lubricant-Infused Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The icing on transmission lines seriously threatens the safe operation of power system. Liquid-infused surfaces (LIS) shows a great potential in the anti-icing field due to its extremely low ice-adhesion strength. Herein, the freezing time, frost morphology, anti-icing performance under glaze ice, and anti-icing durability of the LIS were systematically studied. 1061 aluminum, the same material as aluminum conductors, was selected as the substrate. The porous surface was prepared by anodic oxidation, and the LIS was prepared by infusing silicone oil into the porous structure. The freezing time of the LIS at −8 °C was 1890 s, which was about 7 times that of the bare. The frost weight of the LIS at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.0 h$</tex> was 120.5 mg, which was much lower than that of bare. Under the glaze icing, sparse ice particles appeared on the LIS at 3.0 h, while, a dense ice layer appeared on the bare after 2.0 h. Finally, the LIS showed low ice-adhesion strength, only 1.5 % of that of bare. The LIS maintained extremely low ice-adhesion strength (<20.0 kPa) during 20 icing/deicing cycles. Therefore, compared with the bare surface, the LIS show significant icing and frosting delay, excellent anti-icing performance and anti-icing durability. This work provides valuable information for anti-icing applications of LIS in transmission lines.

articleTitle: Effect of Gamma Irradiation on Structure and Electrical Properties of PP Copolymer Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polypropylene (PP) is known as a very sensitive material to gamma radiations (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> -rays). In this study the performances of a copolymer of PP are evaluated. In the field of electrical insulation, one must determine how electrical properties are modified after an irradiation with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{60}\text{Co}$</tex> source and various doses. The effects on the conductivity and space charge distribution under electrical field application are analyzed. During this work, 180 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> -thick films of PP copolymer were exposed to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> -rays in air at room temperature using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{60}\text{Co}$</tex> source (with a dose rate of 23 Gy/min) to reach doses up to 60 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{kGy}$</tex>. Pulsed Electro Acoustic method was used to measure space charge in the sample, at controlled temperature. The protocol was based on 1 h polarization under a DC field (5, 10 and 15 kV/mm) followed by 2 h relaxation. Current measurements were performed under the same polarization conditions but the relaxation was extended to 3 h. DSC analysis showed that while the crystallinity increases after irradiation at 30 kGy, it decreases for 60 kGy dose. On the other hand, at 60 kGy, the thermogram exhibit multiple melting peaks instead of one observed on the virgin sample and 30 kGy exposed sample. Transient charging currents decrease monotonically and rise slightly with dose. PEA measurements show that homocharges are the principal feature of space charge nature in irradiated sample compared to virgin one, even if it was barely noticeable. It appears that, for electrical properties, the PP copolymer exhibits a good resistance to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> -rays in the explored dose range, even if a non-negligible change was detected in the crystallinity. This particular feature needs more explorations to better understand the structure-properties relationships.

articleTitle: Space Charge Research on LDPE in Thermal Waves at Ultra-low temperatures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The effect of thermal waves caused by overcurrent on the space charge accumulation characteristics of the insulation at ultra-low temperatures is still unknown. This article investigates the space charge accumulations of LDPE under different thermal waves and 40 kV/ mm at ultra-low temperatures. The test temperatures are controlled synergistically by the heating rod and liquid nitrogen. LDPE barely accumulates charge at ultra-low temperatures, but charge buildup is obvious under thermal waves. The LDPE accumulates homocharge on the high-temperature side. On the low-temperature side, it accumulates heterocharge first, and then becomes homocharge after temperature stabilization. The electric field inside the sample increases slightly. The lower the initial temperature, the less charge accumulates inside the sample. After the recovery of temperature, the positive charge accumulated in the anode increases slightly. Moreover, the charge accumulated in the LDPE is frozen inside the sample and cannot be dissipated.

articleTitle: Electrical Tree Growth in Epoxy Resin with Metal Filing Inclusions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper investigates the characteristics and behaviors of electrical tree growth of treeing samples of epoxy resin with metal filings inclusions. The location of the filing varied among the samples, with one being near the needle tip, another in the middle of the insulation gap, and the third in contact with the counter-electrode. The study utilizes Phase-Resolved Partial Discharge (PRPD), Pulse Sequence analysis (PSA) and analysis based on partial discharge (PD) waveform parameters to analyze experimental data from the three samples. The findings reveal significant differences in partial discharge patterns and waveform parameters depending on the position of the inclusion. Additionally, our findings revealed that the technique used for sample preparation significantly influences both the behavior of PD and the structure of electrical trees. The observed impact of imperfections on PD activity suggests their potential use in monitoring and assessing tree growth. However, further investigations involving different types of imperfections are required to provide a comprehensive analysis and broaden our understanding in this field.

articleTitle: Impedance Frequency Analysis of Stator Winding of Electric Motors using High-Frequency Equivalent Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study aims to develop a technique for simulating high-frequency circuit to estimate the voltage distribution within the winding when surge voltages enter the stator insulation system of rotating electric motors. The motor under consideration in this paper is a three-phase induction motor with a rated output of 75 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{kW}$</tex> and a rated voltage of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\text{kV}$</tex>. The winding consists of two parallel wound type with 10 turns and 16 windings per phase featuring 4 poles. To measure distributed voltage at any point, the three-phase winding and neutral were disconnected, and measurement leads were attached to each turn winding. By analyzing the structure and arrangement of the motor stator windings, circuit constants including the resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>, selfinductance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>, mutual inductance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>, and capacitance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> were determined. Using these circuit constants, a lumped constant highfrequency circuit model was constructed. the frequency characteristics of impedance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z(f)$</tex> of the winding were obtained by performing transient analysis simulations with LT-Spice software. The calculated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z(f)$</tex> values were then compared against the measured ones of the actual stator winding, validating the highfrequency circuit model. The results indicated a good agreement between the calculated and measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z(f)$</tex> values, suggesting the reliability of the developed high-frequency circuit model for the subject motor.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effect of Temperature on the Reliability of Determining the Insulation State of Transformers by the FDS Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The paper addresses diagnostic methods for assessing the insulation condition of power oil transformers. These methods include measuring insulation resistance, analyzing time responses of voltage and current, and utilizing frequency dielectric spectroscopy (FDS). Additionally, the study presents a detailed interpretation of dielectric response measurements in the frequency domain. The experimental section focuses on measurements conducted on a 25/6 kV traction oil transformer located outdoors. The primary challenge during these measurements is accurately determining the machine's temperature. The paper further includes a mathematical analysis of the error involved in assessing capacity and loss factor when temperature determination is inaccurate. The analysis highlights that the reliability of the FDS method is significantly influenced by correctly determining the temperature.

articleTitle: Use of Kramers-Kronig Transform and Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann Equation to Probe the Molecular Dynamics of Polyamide 10.10 Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: A fundamental knowledge of polymer-nanoparticle interactions, and their impact on polymer dynamics, is essential for successfully achieving the desired characteristics of polymer nanocomposites. Within that scope, broadband dielectric spectroscopy (BDS) was used as a tool to investigate the effect of different 2D materials, i.e., graphene oxide (GO), hexagonal-boron nitride (h-BN), and molybdenum disulfide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{MoS}_{2})$</tex> on the molecular dynamics of polyamide 10.10 (PA 1010) nanocomposites at extremely low contents. It was verified that the 2D materials increase the activation energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(E_{a})$</tex> of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> process in PA 1010, which indicates that the molecular dynamics are restricted by the two-dimensional structure of such particles. This is further evidenced by changes in the shape of the dielectric loss curve during interfacial polarization, which was enhanced for the nanocomposites.

articleTitle: Electrical Evaluation of 30 Years Operation 6.6 kV XLPE Cables Depending on Installation Location
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: As the number of AC XLPE cables operated for more than 30 years increases, interest in aging evaluation of insulation materials is increasing. Therefore, it is necessary to study the insulation characteristics of old cables in order to determine the replacement time of aging AC XLPE cables. However, the prediction of residual life in power distribution cables is arduous due to the difficulty in managing their operating history. In this paper, the electrical characteristics of 30 years operation 6.6 kV XLPE cables were evaluated according to the installation location in the power station. Tan delta test was performed on a 6.6 kV XLPE cable operated for 30 years depending on the installation location. After analyzing the measurement data and classifying them into safety and warning levels, the XLPE cable was peeled to conduct dielectric breakdown tests on the specimens. The XLPE cable installed in the boiler feed pump exhibits higher Tan δ and lower breakdown voltage compared to other locations, indicating a more progressed state of degradation. The cable of the de-heater booster pump showed excellent performance with a low Tan delta value and high dielectric strength. The cables installed in the cooling tower showed both non-degraded and deteriorated cables.

articleTitle: Electrical Trees Grown from Micron-Scale Artificial Channels Fabricated by 2PP 3D Printing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper reports on early-stage exploration into a new method for fabrication of micron-scale voids in polymers for electrical tree testing. A state-of-the-art 3D print technique, two-photon polymerization (2PP) lithography, was employed to print artificial channels of 4 μm in diameter. The channel was printed into a traffic-cone-shaped structure including a needle shaped void for a traditional needle electrode to sit in. The needle was glued to the cone and then cast into epoxy resin cube to form a needle-plane geometry with 2 mm insulation distance. Electrical trees grew from the artificial channel at low voltages, while a higher voltage was required to drive the tree structure to extend beyond the printed traffic cone into epoxy resin. This fabrication technique will allow experiments to determine the sensitivity of tree formation to micron scale voids in polymers.

articleTitle: Measurement of surface charge distribution on DC-GIS cone-type spacer in charge accumulation/decay process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Surface charge accumulation under high DC electric fields causes electric field distortion and flashover voltage reduction in DC gas-insulated switchgear (DC-GIS). Since most studies have investigated the charge accumulation phenomena with disk-type spacers, the phenomena with cone-type spacers are poorly understood. In this study, surface charge density distribution on a downsized cone-type spacer in DC-GIS simulated environment is obtained. Our measured results show that homocharges accumulate dominantly on both surfaces of cone-type spacers, which is the same as the results obtained with disk-type spacers. The experimental results agreed well with the simulated results of resistive field calculation around an inner electrode. We attributed the agreement to the fact that charge transport in the cone-type spacer is dominant by that through spacer bulk due to its cone-shaped structure. This study suggests the validity of the resistive field calculation for insulation designs of cone-type spacers.

articleTitle: Electrical and Mechanical Properties of Electrospun PVDF-HFP with ZrO2 Nanoparticles Used as Separator in Electrochemical Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study focuses on the preparation of nanocomposite polymer separators by the electrospinning technique. PVDF-HFP polymer was combined with different concentrations of ZrO2 (0, 5, 7, and 10 wt%). The fabricated nanofibrous mats were analyzed to evaluate their electrochemical and mechanical properties. The incorporation of the ceramic filler was investigated to determine its influence on the separator performance, aiming to develop high-performance separators for future Energy Storage Systems (ESSs).

articleTitle: Mathematical Model for Numerical Simulations of Relaxor Ferroelectric and Antiferroelectric Fillers for Nonlinear Refractive Field Control Materials in High-Voltage Insulation Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: As a result of their special polarization behavior antiferroelectric (AFE) and relaxor ferroelectric (RFE) materials are promising materials for nonlinear refractive field control in future AC insulation systems, especially in gas insulated systems (GIS). Their unique switchable dielectric behavior enables the design of even more compact power supply components. To identify potential applications of these materials, their functionality was investigated by FEM simulations. For this purpose, a mathematical model based on the polarization properties (P-E-curve) of RFE and AFE material was implemented by using the interface between MATLAB and COMSOL Multiphysics®. To verify the theoretical model, epoxy resin samples with different filler concentrations of lead-free RFE (sodium bismuth titanate) and lead-free AFE (sodium niobate) were prepared, their nonlinear dielectric properties characterized and compared with the results of the FEM simulations.

articleTitle: Lifetime Analysis of the Insulation System of Traction Machines Based on the Partial Discharge Behavior of Hairpin Wire Pairs and Conventional Twisted Wire Pairs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: There are many investigations regarding the lifetime behavior of conventional enameled twisted wire pairs (CTP). CTPs are chosen to imitate the winding insulation of a machine with round wire winding. However, in automotive traction machines, flat wires with a rectangular cross-section (hairpins) are mostly used. Since the geometry of the wires determines the electric field distribution and its degree of non-uniformity, it has a significant effect on the partial discharge (PD) behavior. There is no detailed publication yet that compares CTPs with hairpin wire pairs (HWP) in terms of lifetime analysis at pulsed voltage with very steep switching slopes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(^{\mathrm{d}v}/\mathrm{d}t)$</tex> using wide band gap (WBG) semiconductor devices such as silicon carbide (SiC). The in-depth analysis will show that the PD and lifetime behavior of the HWP differs significantly from CTP.
